summary: Built SL-020 from an empty tree: an SDK 10 solution (FsAnalyser.slnx, global.json pinning 10.0.100 with latestFeature, and eng/dotnet.ps1, which installed SDK 10.0.401 into a gitignored .dotnet/), the Core scanner (Native/LongPath, DirectoryReader over FILE_ID_EXTD_DIR_INFO with a whole-scan FILE_FULL_DIR_INFO fallback, a tag-only EntryClassifier, SizeProbe for WOF suspects and first FileId repeats, a depth-first Scanner, and a paged struct-of-arrays ScanStore with a custom open-addressing FileId index), and the WPF window (drive row, OpenFolderDialog, optional path argument, polled progress, Cancel, and three different endings: Finished, Stopped, Could not read). There are 72 xUnit tests, none skipped. They build real NTFS trees in %TEMP% for every counting rule, and a synthetic test puts 5M entries in the store: it retains 555.9 MiB and peaks at 569.9 MiB. All 72 pass. Through its path argument the app read the whole of C:\ in 129.4 s (3,435,410 files, 665,497 folders, 16,864 links not followed, 599 unreadable folders listed) at a 581 MiB peak. The single-file self-contained publish (133 MiB exe) runs on a machine with no .NET 10 runtime.

files.why: Pins SDK 10.0.100 with rollForward latestFeature, so a bare 9.0 `dotnet` fails loudly instead of building on 9.
Uses a machine-wide 10.0 SDK if one exists. Otherwise it runs dotnet-install.ps1 -Channel 10.0 into .dotnet/ as the ordinary user (per Q-003), then forwards all arguments. It never falls back to 9.0.
Ignores .dotnet/, bin/, obj/, TestResults/ and IDE state.
net10.0-windows, nullable and implicit usings for all three projects.
SDK 10 solution format with Core, App and Core.Tests.
Core library: AllowUnsafeBlocks (Core only), InternalsVisibleTo for the test project, no WPF.
LibraryImport of CreateFileW and GetFileInformationByHandleEx, plus the info-class, attribute, tag and error constants. Production calls only.
Normalises the root once (bare C: becomes C:\, relative paths throw), maps it to \\?\ or \\?\UNC\, joins children by plain concatenation, and converts back to display form.

Opens one directory handle (FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY, backup semantics, no OPEN_REPARSE_POINT) and pages the RestartInfo-then-Info classes through a 64 KiB aligned buffer, at the spike-verified offsets. Returns the Win32 error together with the entries already read.
The only reader of the reparse bit. Link means tag 0xA0000003 or 0xA000000C. CloudOnly means a file with RECALL_ON_DATA_ACCESS, RECALL_ON_OPEN or OFFLINE.
Opens with FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES only and reads FILE_STANDARD_INFO. Holds the WOF-suspect guard (AllocationSize 0, EOF >= 4096, not sparse, not cloud).

Scan(root, progress, ct): checks the root is a directory (else 267), picks the listing class once (1/50/87 switch to full-dir), walks depth-first with an explicit stack, appends each listing contiguously, deduplicates hardlinks, probes, records unreadable folders, and checks cancellation once per folder.
The internal test seam: ForceFullDirectoryClass and AfterFolder.
Polled counters with a single writer (Volatile), plus CurrentFolder in display form.
ScanStatus, ScanTotals, UnreadableFolder, and ScanResult (Status, Root, RootError, Store, Totals, Unreadable, ProbeFailures, FileIdsAvailable, Elapsed, and an internal Probes count).
EntryKind (Folder/File/Link) and EntryFlags (Unreadable, HardlinkDuplicate, CloudOnly, SizeProbed, ProbeFailed).

Struct-of-arrays store in fixed 65,536-entry pages and 1M-char name pages. Page directories are preallocated, so nothing moves or doubles. No per-entry objects; paths are rebuilt from Parent. The FileId index is a custom open-addressing int[] table keyed through the columns. Reads are public, writes internal, and size corrections are in-place volatile 8-byte writes.
WPF WinExe with ServerGarbageCollection=false, win-x64, SelfContained, PublishSingleFile, IncludeNativeLibrariesForSelfExtract, no trimming.
Application with a Startup handler.
Passes the optional first command-line argument to the window as the path to scan at launch.
Picker panel (drive row plus 'Choose a folder...'), scanning panel (indeterminate bar, counters, current folder, Cancel), and outcome panel (title, totals, notes, unreadable-folder expander).

Code-behind only. Drives are read off the UI thread through DriveInfo. OpenFolderDialog. The scan runs through Task.Factory.StartNew(LongRunning), a 250 ms DispatcherTimer polls progress, and pickers are disabled during a scan. The previous result is dropped before a new scan. The three endings are coloured differently, with FileId and probe-failure notes.
Generated by `dotnet new xunit` under SDK 10.0.401 (xunit 2.9.3, runner 3.1.4, Test.Sdk 17.14.1), retargeted by Directory.Build.props, with a Core reference.

Real NTFS trees under %TEMP%\fsa-tests\<guid>: symlinks through .NET, junctions and hardlinks through mklink, sparse files (write flushed), compact /c and /exe:xpress4k, raw-mask deny ACEs through SDDL, and outside-the-root folders. Dispose restores ACLs, then removes links, then trees, and throws if anything leaked.
Test-only FSCTL_SET_SPARSE through DeviceIoControl.
Helpers: run a scan, map paths to entries, get a raw DirectoryReader listing, and find entries under links.
Cases 1 and 2: nested, empty, zero-byte and hidden+system entries; about 2,000 100-character names over several 64 KiB buffers.
Case 3 (page and name-page rollover), bounds, GetPath, and FileId index growth. Also the O-001 5M-entry memory-fit test, in a non-parallel collection.
A 21-row table from the spike's tag tally plus the RECALL/OFFLINE attributes.
Case 4 on a real tree (a 400+ character path with a 255-character component, 'dot.', 'space ', NUL), plus the root, UNC, child and display mappings.
Case 5: junctions, directory symlinks and file symlinks pointing outside, inside and at an ancestor, plus a dangling one. All recorded as Link, charged 0 bytes, never entered.
Case 6 as one theory (stale name first, three names, reverse order), the documentary stale-listing test, and case 13 (a lone name under the root, recorded limitation).
Case 7 (sparse, LZNT, plain) and case 8 (WOF probed; all-hole sparse, OFFLINE and resident not probed; denied WOF probe keeps the listing value and is counted).
Case 9: a folder with a deny-ListDirectory ACE is flagged Unreadable with error 5, and its siblings are counted.
Case 10: a regular file (267), a missing path (2), bare C: (the drive root, not the cwd), relative and empty paths (ArgumentException), and a junction picked as the root.
Case 11: cancel after the third folder through AfterFolder, and an already-cancelled token.
Case 12: forced FILE_FULL_DIR_INFO on real NTFS gives the same entries and counts, no FileIds, no dedup, and links still detected from EaSize.

obligations.how: The recorded answer is truncated at 900 characters in the engine DB. I read that text read-only from engine.db (decisions.note 898 / obligations.discharge_note 267) to recover rules (a)-(c). (a) Every column is a fixed 65,536-entry page and names go into fixed 1M-char pages. The page directories are preallocated at full size, so there is no List<T> or Array.Resize in the store. (b) There is no per-entry object: names are pooled UTF-16 and GetPath rebuilds paths from Parent. (c) The FileId index is a custom open-addressing, linear-probing int[] of entry indices (splitmix64 hash read from the FileId columns, load <= 70%). It is not a BCL HashSet or Dictionary. It is the one structure that rehashes as it grows (8,388,608 slots = 32 MiB at 4.3M IDs). The fit test is ScanStoreBudgetTests.FiveMillionEntriesFitTheMemoryBudget, using U-001's shape (5M entries, 4.5M files, mean name about 26.5 chars, 4.3M distinct IDs with 300k names sharing 100k). It measured 555.9 MiB retained and a 569.9 MiB sampled peak against an 800 MiB store budget, which leaves room for U-001's roughly 160 MB WPF share. The real app scan of C:\ (4.1M entries) peaked at 581 MiB paged.

tests.note: First build step as the design required. No 10.0 SDK was on the machine, so the script downloaded dotnet-sdk-10.0.401-win-x64.zip (300,608,304 B) into .dotnet/ and printed 10.0.401, exit 0. This settles the dotnet10-in-builder-context no-go through the bootstrap.

First run: 73 of 74 passed. SparseCompressedAndPlainFilesTakeTheListingsOnDiskSize failed with the sparse file's OnDisk = 0. A throwaway diagnostic test showed that both the listing and a FILE_STANDARD_INFO handle report 0 allocated until the 4 KiB write is flushed, and both report 65,536 after Flush(true). The fixture now flushes. The scanner is unchanged. The diagnostic file was deleted.
The throwaway sparse and LZNT experiment above (LZNT listing alloc 524,288 of 4 MiB = probe). The file was removed afterwards.
74/74 after the fixture fix. Budget test output: retained 555.9 MiB, sampled peak 569.9 MiB, 8,388,608 FileId slots, 200,000 duplicate names.

Final full run after merging the hardlink orders into one theory and the case-8 shapes into one test: Total 72, Passed 72, no Skipped. %TEMP%\fsa-tests was left with 0 entries (no leaked trees or ACEs).

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests --filter "FullyQualifiedName~FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.<each case filter>"
tests.note: All 15 per-case and obligation filter commands listed in `cases` (plus the documentary stale-listing and budget tests) were run one by one. Each exited 0 with Passed >= 1: 1 test each, 3 for the hardlink theory, 7 for RootTests, 2 for CancellationTests.

tests.command: Start-Process src/FsAnalyser.App/bin/Debug/net10.0-windows/win-x64/FsAnalyser.App.exe <folder | missing path | relative\folder>  (outcome read with UIAutomationClient)
tests.note: Finished: 2 files and 1 folder. Missing path: 'Could not read ... The system cannot find the file specified. (Windows error 2)'. Relative path: 'Could not read relative\folder' with the not-absolute message. The drive row showed C:, D: and Z: with label, format and free space.

tests.command: Start-Process FsAnalyser.App.exe C:\ then Invoke the Cancel button through UI Automation after 4 s
tests.note: During the scan: '1,95,876 files, 26,772 folders, 112.7 GB ... 512 folders unreadable' and the current folder text updated. After Cancel: 'Stopped: C:\. This is only what was read before the stop, not the whole folder.' plus partial totals and the unreadable expander. An earlier launch with the argument quoted as "C:\" reached the app as C:" (Windows argv escaping) and correctly landed in Could not read.

tests.command: Start-Process FsAnalyser.App.exe C:\ and poll until the outcome text appears
tests.note: Full real drive, unelevated: 'Finished: C:\', 3,435,410 files and 665,497 folders, 16,864 links not followed, 952.2 GB in files taking 685.8 GB on disk, read in 129.4 s. 3 probe failures noted, 599 folders could not be read. Process peak paged 581 MiB, peak working set 636 MiB.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 publish src/FsAnalyser.App -c Release -r win-x64 -nologo
tests.note: Single-file self-contained publish produced FsAnalyser.App.exe (133.3 MiB). It was launched from a shell with no DOTNET_ROOT, on a machine with no .NET 10 runtime installed, and reached 'Finished' on a temp folder.

tests.command: Grep of the four architecture-rule patterns over src/FsAnalyser.Core/**, src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/** and tests/**
tests.note: No System.Windows, PresentationFramework or App references and no UseWPF in Core. The reparse-attribute patterns match only EntryClassifier.cs (the excepted file). No System.IO enumerators in Scanning. No Skip in tests.

deviations: Hardlink index: the design says 'a HashSet<int> of entry indices whose comparer reads the FileId columns'. O-001's recorded answer, which is newer and is a person's decision, says rule (c): not a BCL HashSet or Dictionary, but a custom open-addressing table. I built the custom table (int[] of index+1, linear probing, splitmix64 over the FileId columns, rehash at 70% load). The answer outranks the design text written before it.

Denied-probe fixture: the design says deny ACEs use FileSystemAclExtensions with the current user's SID. Measured on this PC: a deny ReadAttributes rule does not stop a FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES open (error 0), because NTFS grants it through the parent's FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY. FileSystemAccessRule also strips SYNCHRONIZE from deny rules. So TempTree.Deny still goes through Get/SetAccessControl but writes the ACE as SDDL with a raw mask. SYNCHRONIZE|FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES (0x100080) makes the probe fail with error 5.

Sparse fixture: the design's '4 KiB written in 64 MiB' file must be flushed (FlushFileBuffers) before scanning. Until it is, NTFS itself reports 0 allocated through both the listing and an opened handle, so no scanner could see the allocation. The scanner and the 'listing is trusted for sparse' rule are unchanged.
The design writes App.csproj as pinning 'ServerGarbageCollector=false'. The MSBuild property is ServerGarbageCollection, and that is what is set.

Contract additions: ScanResult.Root (public), the normalised root, because the 'Could not read' state names the root and the UI needs its normalised form. Also internal ScanResult.Probes and ScanStore.FileIdTableSlots, visible only to tests. They let the tests prove the third hardlink name and the OFFLINE, sparse and resident files are never probed. The public read API is otherwise exactly the design's list.

Two semantics the design left implicit, now fixed in code and doc comments. Totals count entries under the root, not the root itself. CloudOnly is set only on File entries: a folder carrying RECALL attributes is a Folder and is entered, per the design's 'every other reparse directory is entered'. An already-cancelled token returns Cancelled with an empty store (Count 0) and does no I/O.
not_built: The test-local CreateSymbolicLinkW with SYMBOLIC_LINK_FLAG_ALLOW_UNPRIVILEGED_CREATE. The design names it as the fix only 'if 1314 ever appears'. File and Directory.CreateSymbolicLink worked unelevated in every run (LinkTests and ListingFallbackTests pass), so it was not needed.
follow_ups: The architecture's Scan Engine asks the volume for used space on a whole-drive scan, to show the coverage gap. This slice's design has no component for it. On C: this run found 685.8 GB on disk against about 735 GB used, with 599 unreadable folders. That gap is what the coverage panel would show.

A bare `dotnet` in this repo now fails, deliberately: global.json pins 10.0.100 and the machine has only 9.0.318. Every build, test and publish must go through eng/dotnet.ps1. Each fresh worktree downloads about 300 MB into its own .dotnet/ unless someone installs a 10.0 SDK machine-wide once (Q-003's stated escape).

Cases C-010 and C-011 are fed by class-level filters (RootTests.: 7 tests; CancellationTests.: 2 tests) because each case bundles several distinct shapes. If the engine needs exactly one method per case, those two classes could become single tests.

U-001 measured WPF's share at about 160 MB, and the 800 MiB store budget in ScanStoreBudgetTests is derived from that. When the tree slice adds the virtualized view, re-measure the whole app at 5M entries against 1 GiB.
The unreadable-folder list builds every path when a scan ends (599 on C:). Fine at this size. The later unreadable panel may want to build paths lazily.
SL-020 is still stored with risk_tier 'low' in the engine DB (slices row 36), although Q-002 decided to raise it to medium. Re-tiering is the engine's step, not this build's.
